title: fully ai generated outdoor secen
author: zenmatrix83
selftext: Its a walkable godot level, you can go in the cabin, there is particle effects for smoke. I'm struggling with the walls and the color balance but the entire thing is 100% ai, trellis, comfy, lots of python scripts, and headless blender. Mostly its skills and agents that read checklists create and review the scene from multiple locations, do image analysis on each image, and run filters on each image trying to find problems. Its supposed to check color balance and other things, but there is a slight wash out, but playing it is slightly worse zelda bow or maybe weak skyrim level graphics

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: Trellis is on a 4090 plus Claude doing post work and running custom scripts on them. I’m trying a bunch of scenes getting some generic workflows and doing more. I can get decent terrain and grass consistently, but the cliffs take hours of attempts to make improvements . The early attempts it just wanted to pile up rocks. I have Claude code use comfy ui to generate reference images and compare to the assets which helps a lot.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body:
this was a doc claude generated that I think has everything. It a mix ff scattering the mesh, but past this was finding a grass texture that blended with with the mode. I just fed claude examples we downloaded screeenshots and had it figgure it out. From some of my previous attempts I also had it create slope maps based of how steep the terrain is and the steper the terrain is the less grass is there, steep parts also get a rock texture.

    # Larkspur Vale — Grass Look-Plan (AAA-target rebuild)
    
    
    The user's #1 gripe with Hollowmere was the grass: 
    **density, shape, color.**
     This is the spec for the
    grass rebuild, synthesized from (a) AAA research — Ghost of Tsushima GDC 2021 (the canonical per-blade
    grass talk), KCD2 (per-blade SSS + GI), FF7 Rebirth, Crimson Desert (wind cautionary tale), UE5 Nanite
    foliage budgets — and (b) our own pinned references (`reference/groundcover/…s5`, `…/slope-transition/…s17`).
    
    
    Improve the grass 
    **generically**
     in `blender/ops/grass_clump.py` + `ground_cover.py` (feed Larkspur's
    palette/density as DATA — the project-agnostic HARD RULE; `build_clump` already takes colour/shape knobs
    and `ground_cover(layers=…)` is parameterized). Iterate in isolation with `blender/ops/grass_preview.py`
    and 
    **eye-level-verify vs the references**
     before it enters the assembly.
    
    
    ## The 7 things that make AAA grass read premium (ranked)
    
    
    1. 
    **Clumping, not uniform scatter**
     — blades cluster in patches of a species with barer gaps between;
       kills both "even lawn" and "sparse tufts on dirt" at once. (GoT drives height/bend/facing/color off a
       Voronoi clump field.)
    2. 
    **Curved, tapered blades**
     — cubic-Bézier-style bow with a rest-bend, not flat rectangles.
    3. 
    **Color variation at 3 scales**
     — tip↔base gradient × per-clump tint × per-blade jitter.
    4. 
    **Backlit translucency (SSS)**
     — the inner glow "sells the nature render" (KCD2).
    5. 
    **Grounding into terrain**
     — base AO, blade base tinted toward soil, dark ground under grass, no hard
       intersection line.
    6. 
    **Believable wind**
     — stiff base / floppy tip, per-blade phase, slow gust + tiny tip flutter. Keep
       amplitude LOW (Crimson Desert's over-driven wind is mocked as "foliage having a seizure").
    7. 
    **Density falloff → texture handoff**
     — dense near, thinning out, then the terrain ground-texture
       carries the far field (no shimmering blade horizon).
    
    
    ## Targets for the three pain points
    
    
    ### DENSITY
    - 
    **Near field (0–5 m): a fully CLOSED clumped carpet — no continuous bare soil visible.**
     AAA near-camera
      is ~2,000–10,000 blades/m². Our unit is a clump (tuft); Hollowmere ran `grass density_max=9.0` clumps/m²
      × ~8–11 blades = ~70–100 blades/m² → reads sparse. 
    **Raise it hard.**
    - 
    **Two-layer scatter:**
     (1) a dense short 
    **carpet**
     layer that closes the ground plane + (2) a sparser
      
    **tall emergent**
     layer (taller grass + seed-head stalks) sitting in the carpet for silhouette.
    - 
    **Patchiness via low-freq noise:**
     strengthen the low-frequency term of the density noise stack so clumps
      cluster into patches with barer gaps — not the near-even Poisson lattice. Bare-ground near camera <~10–15%
      and only where motivated (stream edge, rock bases, the walkable desire-line).
    - 
    **Bands:**
     full 0–5 m; thinning 5–~30 m; 
    **terrain grass-albedo carries >~30 m**
     (the height-ramp
      material's green band is our far-field handoff — make sure it reads as grass, not flat green).
    
    
    ### SHAPE
    - 
    **Curved tapered blade cards**
    : bump `segments` 2→3–4 so the blade bows; keep the quadratic droop; model a
      
    **rest-bend**
     (blades bowed even with no wind — dead-straight reads synthetic).
    - 
    **More blades/clump**
     (carpet clumps denser) and a real 
    **form mix**
     — don't ship one blade type:
      - fine narrow grass (the carpet bulk),
      - 
    **tall seed-head / flowering stalks**
     (thin emergents with a tan seed tip — big readability boost,
        catches backlight; visible as the tan stalks in `…groundcover…s5`),
      - a 
    **broader-leaf forb/clover**
     form (visual weight, breaks needle monotony),
      - 
    **dry/dead blades**
     mixed in (see COLOR).
    - 
    **Clump-driven height variation**
     so tall/short cluster naturally (not salt-and-pepper).
    
    
    ### COLOR  (the critical one — and re-tuned for MIDDAY, not Hollowmere's golden lime)
    Grass hue target = the 
    **vivid healthy spring-green**
     of `…groundcover…s5` / `…slope-transition…s17`
    (cool-to-mid green, saturated but not lime), NOT the golden-tawny of `…establishing…s7` (that's the
    DISTANT / drier upper-slope grass, delivered by aerial perspective + the terrain ramp).
    - 
    **(a) tip↔base gradient**
     per blade: base cooler/darker (shadowed root), tip lighter, 
    *slightly*
     warmer,
      a touch desaturated (where backlight glows through).
    - 
    **(b) per-clump tint**
    : 3–5 clump colour variants spread yellow-green → mid-green → a few blue-greens, so
      neighbouring patches differ (breaks "one green" into a patchwork). Widen from Hollowmere's ±0.05 hue.
    - 
    **(c) per-blade jitter**
    : small extra hue/value per blade so no two adjacent match.
    - 
    **(d) dead/dry blades ~15–25%**
     (alpine early-summer, lean toward the lower end since s5 is lush) — a
      straw/tan ramp routed to a fraction of blades 
    *and*
     some whole clumps browner.
    - 
    **(e) backlit translucency**
     tinted slightly 
    **warm-gold**
     so tips glow, not flat green; only reads with
      the sun behind — verify with a backlit test even though the hero is midday.
    - 
    **(f) aerial perspective**
    : distant grass desaturates, lifts in value, cools toward blue-grey (height fog
      + compositor in `world_beauty`, not the material). Dither the large gradient to kill banding.
    
    
    **Larkspur midday palette (starting numbers — tune against s5):**
    | role | base RGB | tip RGB |
    |---|---|---|
    | healthy grass (carpet) | `(0.05, 0.14, 0.055)` | `(0.34, 0.55, 0.22)` (greener/less yellow than Hollowmere's `0.40,0.50,0.20`) |
    | dry/straw blade (~20%) | `(0.20, 0.16, 0.06)` | `(0.60, 0.52, 0.24)` |
    | seed-head stalk | green `(0.10, 0.20, 0.07)` | tan seed `(0.55, 0.48, 0.22)` |
    | per-clump tint spread | hue ±0.10–0.12 (was ±0.05), value 0.75–1.15 | |
    | saturation | ~0.95 (allow more than Hollowmere's 0.90 — midday grass is saturated; keep green ch dominant + blue ch present to avoid lime) | |
    | translucency mix | ~0.20, warm-gold tint `(0.32, 0.42, 0.14)` | |
    
    
    ## Lighting / grounding / wind
    - 
    **SSS/translucency**
    : Translucent BSDF (or Principled subsurface random-walk) mixed for backlit glow;
      small radius, warm-gold transmission. glTF `KHR_materials_transmission` stays on as the engine cue.
    - 
    **Base AO**
    : multiply a darkening gradient by model-space blade height (self-AO of the carpet).
    - 
    **Grounding**
    : tint blade base toward terrain soil colour; ensure terrain-under-grass albedo is a DARK
      ground, not bright dirt, so no intersection line. (The height-ramp material's low band should read soil.)
    - 
    **Wind**
    : one shared scrolling-noise gust driving bend + facing; bend weighted to the tip (stiff base);
      per-instance `wind_phase` (already emitted) desyncs neighbours; add a tiny high-freq tip flutter. LOW
      amplitude, slow gust.
    - 
    **Perf**
    : clumps stay GPU-instanced (never realize millions of blades); cap grass-material samples; no
      shader-Bevel on the grass (known GPU-deadlock risk); watch self-shadow cost.
    
    
    ## Map to our current code
    - `grass_clump.py`: `BASE_RGB`/`TIP_RGB`, `GREEN_FLOOR`, `TRANSLUCENT_RGB` (re-tune to the table above);
      `_blade` (segments/rest-bend), `build_clump` (blades/clump, form knobs); `apply_grass_shader` +
      `_grass_instance_variation` (widen hue/value spread, add dry-blade route + base-AO + warm SSS).
    - `ground_cover.py`: `_LAYERS` (raise grass `density_max`/`cover`, add a tall-emergent + seed-head layer,
      strengthen low-freq patchiness in `_density_factor`'s noise stack); `_grass_templates` (more blades,
      add seed-head + forb + dry templates); `FLOWER_VARIANTS` keep the s5 blue larkspur/forget-me-not +
      yellow buttercup + white daisy.
    - Verify with `grass_preview.py` at 
    **eye level**
    , backlit + midday, 1:1 vs `…groundcover…s5`.
    
    
    ## Sources (best close-up breakdowns)
    GoT GDC 2021: gdcvault.com/play/1027033 · tigerabrodi.blog/grass-in-ghost-of-tsushima ·
    github.com/2Retr0/GodotGrass · KCD2: gamegpu KCD2 benchmark · Creative Shrimp translucent-grass ·
    Blender Artists thin-translucency · StraySpark Nanite-foliage guide (density/LOD budgets) ·
    80.lv Nanite dense-grass (483k instances).

comments.author: mouseGRENADE
comments.body: I’m not sure how this didn’t get more traction, this is fantastic. Are you able to go a little more into the process with the skills and agents?

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body:
there is alot of skills and agents, and there are also check lists and other documenation files directly mentioned in skills and agents. The general flow is trellis creates a mesh, it goes through a asset workshop with color filters and stuff looking for issues, one turns the background purple so the agent can look at screenshot for floating perice for example. Then for animiation it create boards of frames for multiple directions and checks the beginning and ending frames for differences to make sure the animation is seamless. Then the full scene is built, I'm woking on a 4k by 4k map now doing a tile at a time, but the sameprocess is used for a tile a time. In planning I just started having it create 2 maps for mapping for vegatation water slop and a bunch of other things. Anytime I get stuck we update checklists, create or redit skills and agents and move on. If it seems structural I just start over. I can build this scene in a few hours now, claude just does what I need for the most part on its own, it just gives me images to approve now and then. It does more then this, just from yesterday there are 50 or so qa images its been updating  from different spots.
